clauses.rationale: All four generated validated event streams retain default validation; current whole-service conformance executes their validation and forward/replay checks.
Generated nominal witnesses retain complete Text domains; structural queue enums have exhaustive shape fixtures. No hand-built projection or constructor literal exists.
Behavior reports preserve unverified identity guards. No consumer wraps unknown/opaque solver results as proof. No opaque collection/arithmetic guard exists; no opt-in opaque result is claimed.
No hand-owned sequential, alternative or feedback Keiki pipeline exists. Each persisted aggregate has its own validated stream; the at-risk machine is diagram-only.
No application compose/composeChecked or non-invertible map adapter claims a structural composition proof. Current source census is recorded in current-domain-contracts.md.
Lifecycle revision and pending-receipt counters stay scalar; membership and rich payload integrity are checked in protected SQL transactions.
No collection register/content guard or TApp membership closure exists in the four generated aggregate transducers. Queue lineage is ordered data, not a guard.
Generated aggregate constructors use released derivation; the hand-owned at-risk nullary command descriptors use mkInCtorVia and Generic.
No unavailable/deprecated constructor producer, manual record construction, relabel adapter or composed input/wire boundary exists in hand-owned application machines.

Execution persistence retains outer event rejection and operational failures separately from typed precondition refusal. The native graph test rejects an unexpected silent edge; no ambiguity can become accepted work.

Generated BehaviorContract executes detailed selected-edge attribution. Failed replay never returns partially hydrated state or a fabricated receipt; current PostgreSQL histories and service witnesses pass.
DomainDiagrams renders all four persisted aggregates plus the sole hand-owned Keiki machine with toMermaid defaults; no transducer orchestrator is omitted.
just domain-diagrams writes source-derived atlas and detailed inspectors with pretty guards and output fields. Six diagram tests validate readable syntax and exact checked-in bytes.
AtRiskCustomer explicitly documents its non-event-source epsilon exception; persisted aggregates never disable that check. OpenTelemetry has a static workflow diagram, not a Keiki machine.
RunJobs has one complete current version-1 envelope with no obsolete upcasters. Four aggregate codecs remain generated with their explicit wire policy.
ADR-27 four-fact unused-service reset has no historical consumer. Strict breaking reports are retained. No old defaults, retired events or upcaster chains are invented for an empty population.
WireCompatSpec rejects obsolete envelopes and omitted current required nullable fields; current positive bytes, execution metadata and ordered lineage round-trip.
Three nominal Text isomorphisms are total wrappers/unwrappers, with declared initial and canonical identity. Queue enum shapes are exhaustive total structural bindings.
No one-way application witness is called exact, no empty finite image is supplied, and unverified behavior guards stay unverified. There is no aggregate enum guard requiring a finite equality proof.
All four aggregate codecs are scaffolded and service conformance crosses their encode/decode boundary; no duplicate hand-written private-event codec remains.
Independent execution-event JSON golden retains string identity after nominal adoption. Queue current schema and negative admission vectors are tested; public HTTP/Danwa codecs remain distinct.
AtRiskCustomer uses qualified builder verbs and no shared lens-prelude operators. Generated comparisons are generator-owned; no ambiguous hand-owned import or fixity workaround exists.
Ten workspace members and four aggregate streams are inventoried. All focused Keiki topics have clause dispositions in this inventory, with current validation/replay/diagram evidence.
The service did not consume the removed 0.1 Decider API or old renderer/constructor APIs. Current released generator output compiles; no historical upgrade consumer or old snapshot cache is present.
Production hydration stays in released Keiro runners; current corruption and guard/receipt recovery tests preserve failure boundaries. No Maybe fallback or custom partial fold is added.
Every aggregate BehaviorContract crosses its codec and checks history-backed transitions and register equality; native same-build workflow restart coverage passes.

Current aggregate transitions emit one event each; no application paged replay owns InFlight or a multi-event chain. Detailed attribution is exercised by generated behavior witnesses, not retained on hot paths.
No deployed retired event population exists under ADR-27. No replay-only twin is fabricated; future deployed guard tightening must preserve real history.
Current four aggregates are generated-owned, with explicit guards/writes and fields(Command) events. No application delta-plus-omega runner or whole-transducer hole exists.
Three application identity newtypes replace primitive command/event/register fields. Rich protected payloads remain SQL rows, not register caches; external parsing stays at ingress.
Current generated scalar guards constrain decrements and revisions; default validation remains enabled. No secret literal, opaque arithmetic or collection-content guard is introduced.
All four behavior contracts, native histories, queue wire vectors and source-derived atlas/inspectors pass. No orchestrator transducer or hosted process manager exists to compose.
Three nominal identities use released generated projections; no application getter or nested/projection-in-output workaround exists.
Commands/events/registers retain their complete domain value. Current one-way guard obligations stay unverified; queue structural enums have exhaustive shape/key laws, but no enum guard is claimed.
No Keiki 0.1 source, deprecated Decider facade, old builder/codec construction or live 0.1 snapshot exists. This child consumes released current generated APIs.
Current default validation, structured replay and conservative proof taxonomy are qualified through service conformance; aggregate stateCodec is Nothing, so no old hash is admitted.
Every current transition declares scalar guard/write behavior in the DSL; no hand-owned edge override or obsolete identity-copy hook exists.
Nominal identity register initials use declared consumer symbols. No existing mapped clear/scalar construction transition exists; no total lift is pretended over protected SQL payloads.
Queue trigger/route enums are data-only. Aggregate phases are vertices; no enum-valued guard or native equality adapter exists to replace. Their addition leaves unrelated folds unchanged.
Current scalar revisions/counts and qualified command/register roots compile under strict Language 6. No aliases, Time arithmetic, Int arithmetic or eventless state-changing transition is introduced.
The generated whole-service target runs all four BehaviorContracts; required witnesses are filled and missing/pending/duplicate/stale/failed buckets empty.
Unverified identity guards stay unverified. No blanket fail-on-unverified pressure relabels them; generated total guards and structural/nominal laws execute separately.
Re-scaffolded 0.22 BehaviorContracts expose behaviorObligationReport/coverageReportFor and retain all real application witnesses. Full 159-assertion service conformance passes.

Guarded lifecycle commands preserve tentative-append rollback and no receipt/position on refused work. Current native graph has no silent edge; fallback silently refuses rather than accepting an empty append.

CommandRejected remains EventRejected and store/retry exhaustion are operational failures. All remaining command defects return an error, never accepted business work. Late owner/hook errors retain exception rollback.

Native concurrent identical requests, conflicting inputs, stale claims, lost responses and post-write fault injection retain protected lifecycle/accounting/receipt invariants. Rich payloads remain inside one accepted transaction.
Delivery retry/ack and dead-letter controls remain separate plan94/106 obligations; this row qualifies only execution persistence, not worker or operator policy.
One ten-member versioned collocated workspace is the authority; generated files were changed solely by scaffolding. All components compile with complete generated module inventory.
Queue structural enums and three nominal identity consumers remove real adapters. Current opaque refined/upstream codecs remain where conversion rejects; no false total binding is substituted.

FRIC-9 current required-nullable queue wrapper remains because released top-level optional fields are unsupported. Rich live-only SQL payloads, external HTTP and Danwa protocols remain distinct executed owners.
Strict check, bindings, coverage, inspection, scaffold idempotence, exact breaking diff/replay and all service witnesses pass or retain the intended breaking exit. API AST tooling is absent.
Complete Cabal fragment reconciles StructuralConformance and BehaviorSourceMap. Filled application holes/bindings survive regeneration; second scaffold changes zero files.
Strict reports retain both projections and declaration-specific fold comparison. Three nominal consumers change their folds while unrelated RunEvidence is stable.
No hand-written planner/source-index implementation or behavior-key location cache exists. Released CLI owns provenance and stable key mapping.
Current idiomatic-v2 ledger remains authoritative; default concise record APIs and full component compilation pass. No migration backup is deleted or ledger edited to bypass a gate.
All aggregate contracts, harnesses, nominal/structural modules and Cabal inventory are regenerated with pinned DSL0.22. Hand-owned expectation changes were semantically reviewed before updating.
This candidate does not change edition or move sidecar names, so no edition apply/rollback occurs. Ordinary idempotence proves only current output, not historical backup contents.
RunEvidenceId retains generated abstract TypeID-v7 admission. Current domain parser and malformed-ID tests remain active; no raw internal replay constructor is introduced.
Execution/worker-session/objective technical coordinates now preserve actual newtypes via nominal Text isomorphisms. They are not prefix-bearing TypeID domains; generation/SQL identity is unchanged.
No new v5-or-v7 domain, declared public contract ID/list or ID-keyed map consumer exists. Upstream workflow IDs remain opaque technical identities; no historical domain widening is claimed.
All ten sources explicitly select Language6. CI enforces exact version, declared provenance and truthful candidate metadata rather than stable=true.
Application uses pinned CLI and no Keiro.Dsl library imports, AST constructors, ordinal storage or source-index planner. Released tool owns added cases and abstract checked construction.
Scaffold and strict diff preserve deliberate patch-removal findings against88d4b3e, emitting both JSON reports before exit1. No language downgrade or compatibility graph forgery occurs.
Queue structural enum binding and aggregate nominal bindings are actual runtime consumers; the independent event golden and current queue vectors test both boundaries.
Rejecting names/digests and upstream types remain explicit opaque codecs. No date/set/unrestricted-byte/keyed-map or scalar-write-lift consumer exists; no placeholder declaration counts as adoption.
Three affected aggregate folds move and RunEvidence stays stable; snapshots are disabled. Same-build histories and current first-release codec pass; no old population or drain is invented underADR27.
FRIC-9 still requires the small current input/authority wrapper. Obsolete v1-v3 readers/v4 contract were removed; complete currentv1 producer and consumer are tested together.
DomainBindings wraps/unwraps Text for existing ExecutionId, WorkerSessionId and ObjectiveId with canonical identity, deterministic edge fixtures and declared empty initials.
Generated commands, events and registers carry those types. Stores no longer unpack/repack primitive identity for generated commands; independent string wire golden and whole-service laws pass.
Rejecting smart constructors remain opaque rather than fake nominal. No historical decoder tightening is claimed; the first-release reset retains exact directional reports and per-fold evidence.
Native guard/precondition, concurrent receipts, rebuild fence and post-inline exception rollback qualified by plan93M1/M2.
Remaining runtime delivery/retry review belongs to the delivery child.
Online generation/external-read/repair operations belong to the administrative owner; plan93 does not claim those gates.
Ten complete same-context members have explicit single owners under one workspace. Current flat domain filenames are retained; manifest identity/layout/runtime package are unchanged.
All checks, scaffold, diff and conformance operate on the manifest. Second scaffold reports no changed bytes and preserves filled bindings; all current generated modules compile.
No bare-service conversion, independent same-context scaffold, name-migration apply or ownership move is performed in this candidate. The existing current ledger remains authoritative.
First-release SQL identities and checksum lock are frozen under ADR-27; later changes append entries.
Default tests and the standalone gate reject unqualified object targets and search_path; no application exception remains.
Runtime membership and lock checks reject tampering and unlisted siblings. All current application SQL is transactional; no nontransactional directive consumer exists.
No service Codd ledger, import deployment or legacy reader exists. No import facade or historical checksum equivalence is invented; only fresh provisioning is qualified.
The service migration executable owns the complete plan. Plan/list/check/new require no database credentials; status/verify/up/repair retain the released pg-migrate dispatcher.
Read-only startup verification refuses pending/missing/unknown/drifted history. The independent verify-schema command compares framework and application objects and refuses deliberate live drift.

Fresh provisioning applies Kiroku 0012-0016 and PGMQ 0007 before runtime intake. No populated old ledger, withdrawn-checksum repair, active legacy writer or Codd import exists under the confirmed ADR-27 baseline. Final artifact/deployment procedure belongs to plan 95.
The released framework schema checker is PostgreSQL-18-only; the first-release evidence uses PostgreSQL 18 and does not claim PostgreSQL 17 snapshot qualification.
One service executable composes upstream components, exact-byte compile embedding, runtime source checks, startup verification and independent live-object comparison.
migrationPlan validates the authoritative five-component order and declared dependencies; no competing framework SQL owner remains.
RecompilePlugin and strict manifest embedding remain; runtime source/lock/membership tests independently detect stale-build inputs.

The native suite proves fresh apply, strict verification and AlreadyApplied/no-write repetition through the released advisory-lock runner. No custom migration interpreter or nontransactional application action exists.
The migration library stays independent of core, exports one application component and composes Kiroku, Keiro, Kioku and PGMQ once. Application objects use the shikigami schema.
The migration executable owns DATABASE_URL, output and exit status. Runtime startup uses the identical complete plan read-only and never applies pending work.
Nine normal tests include body lint, exact source/embedded agreement and a source checksum lock. Negative fixtures reject changed payloads, unlisted SQL, path mutation and unqualified DDL.

Eleven native tests exercise all five components, strict startup refusals, no-op repetition, fixture isolation and an explicitly generated application schema snapshot. A disposable added column makes independent live verification fail.

Keiro 0.22/pg-migrate 1.2 own stable ephemeral roots and cleanup. Production does not import test-support. No nested session Left is accepted. Populated old-plan and withdrawn-checksum exercises have no first-release consumer; PostgreSQL 17 is not claimed by this evidence.
